title: Kenya - Transport Sector Support Project and its Additional Financing : Notice of Non-Registration - Request for Inspection
text:
Ramanie Kunanayagam
Chairperson
The Inspection Panel
 IPN REQUEST 22/02

 April 13, 2022

 MEMORANDUM TO THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTORS
 INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT ASSOCIATION

 Request for Inspection

 Kenya: Transport Sector Support Project (P124109) and its Additional Financing
 (P146630) - (Second Request)

 Notice of Non-Registration


Summary

1. In accordance with paragraph 18 of the Resolution 1 of the Inspection Panel (the “Panel”), I
hereby inform you that on March 3, 2022, the Panel received a Request for Inspection (the
“Request”) of the Kenya: Transport Sector Support Project (P124109) and its Additional Financing
(P146630) (the “Project”). This is the second request concerning the Project. The Request
acknowledges the Panel’s previous reports. 2

2. The Request was submitted by Emonyo Yefwe International, a local nongovernmental
organization. Thirteen community members from the area of the Webuye interchange signed the
Request (the “Requesters”). The community members live in the area of the Webuye interchange
in the Project area. The Requesters have not asked the Panel to keep their identities confidential.
However, consistent with its practice, the Panel redacted the names of the community members
signing the Request and their phone numbers.

The Project

3. The Transport Sector Support Project was approved on April 21, 2011, in an amount of
US$300 million equivalent. The Additional Financing was approved on March 26, 2014, in an
amount of US$203.50 million equivalent, and became effective on June 20, 2014.

4. The Project has four components: (i) Support to Kenya National Highways Authority
(KeNHA) to improve roads, roadside facilities and road safety and for institutional strengthening;

  The World Bank Inspection Panel, International Development Association, Resolution No. IDA 2020-0003,

 (ii) Institutional strengthening and capacity building in the transport sector; (iii) Support to Kenya
Airports Authority; and (iv) Support to Kenya Civil Aviation Authority. The Requesters’ concerns
relate to the first component. 3 The first component covers the rehabilitation and improvement of
several road sections in Kenya, including the Kisumu-Kakamega-Webuye-Kitale road section,
which includes the Webuye interchange.

5. The environmental category of the Project is “B”. 4 The Project closed on December 31,
2019.

Background

6. On December 17, 2018, the Panel received a first Request for Inspection raising concerns
about potential harm from the construction of the Webuye interchange financed under the Project.
The first Request raises concerns about, among others, livelihood impact to a group of mobile
traders who were active in the area. These mobile traders were not identified in the original
Resettlement Action Plan (RAP).

7. The Panel registered the Request on January 17, 2019. The Panel determined in its initial
eligibility report that the first Request and Requesters met the technical eligibility criteria set forth
in the Resolution. Following the Panel’s first eligibility report, Management identified in a RAP
Audit that 52 mobile traders were not counted by the time of the cutoff date or compensated during
the RAP implementation. On April 26, 2020, Management updated the Panel that the Bungoma
County Government had identified a suitable parcel of land close to the Webuye interchange which
would be used as a marketplace to house the mobile traders, and that the Bungoma Country
Government had fully paid for and finalized the land title deed on March 4, 2020. A marketplace
was to be built on this parcel of land and stalls and kiosks would be assigned to mobile traders.
Based on the commitments made to address the Requesters concerns, including the acquisition of
land in close proximity to the Webuye interchange to build a market for the mobile traders, the
Panel did not recommend an investigation.

The Request

8. The Panel received the Request on March 3, 2022, from Emonyo Yefwe International, a
local nongovernmental organization. Thirteen community members from the area of the Webuye
interchange signed the Request.

9. The Requesters state that Bungoma County Government fully paid for a plot of land to be
used for the construction of a marketplace where the businesses of 52 mobile traders will be
relocated. They add the Bungoma County Government finalized the land title deed on March 4,
2020, and works were expected to start on July 1, 2020. They state that to date the works have not
started. They ask for the “construction to begin immediately”, threats against them be stopped, and

  World Bank, Management Response to Request for Inspection Panel Review of the Kenya: Transport Sector

Document, March 29, 2011 (the “PAD”), p. i and p. 66, para. 53.

 2
 that the World Bank convenes a meeting between mobile traders and the Bungoma County
Government.

Panel’s Observations and Determination

10. In accordance with its Operating Procedures, 5 the Panel issued a Notice of Receipt on its
website on April 1, 2022. The Panel conducted its due diligence by reviewing the information
contained in the Request and Project documents, as well as by speaking to the Requesters on April
4, 2022, to better understand their concerns.

11. Pursuant to the issuance of the Notice of Receipt, on April 4, 2022, Management informed
the Panel that the construction of the market is still being pursued as per Management’s most recent
update on the Management actions. 6 Management reiterated that land was secured for the
construction of the market in March 2020. According to Management, due to the COVID-19
pandemic, construction of the market could not start and the activity was delayed. Management
added that the COVID-19 pandemic caused a shifting of budgetary priorities to address the
pandemic, and as a result the Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) was not able to obtain
the appropriate budget allocation for the market. This process has now re-started with bidding
expected to commence soon. According to Management, KeNHA and County of Bungoma officials
have decided on the design for the market and initiated stakeholder consultations.

12. In light of the foregoing, and in accordance with the Panel Resolution and its Operating
Procedures, given the Project closed on December 31, 2019, the Panel is not registering the Request
for Inspection.

 Yours Sincerely,




 Ramanie Kunanayagam, Chairperson

Whereas, the third and final eligibility report on the Kenya Transport Sector Support Project and its
Additional Financing, the Inspection Panel did not recommend an investigation.
The Panel did note the willingness of Management and the Borrower to address concerns raised by the
community. Concerning livelihood impact , including the identification of mobile traders and small business
owners who were not appropriately compensated for the temporary impact they suffered during
construction.
That, the relocation of the 52 mobile traders from the Webuye interchange area, would follow ofter the
Bungoma County Government acquires a parcel of land dose to the Webuye interchange where a market
would be built and stalls and kiosks assigned to mobile traders to ply their trade.
That,Management stated that the Bungoma County Government had identified a suitable plot, which it has
fully paid for, and had finalized the land title deed on March 4, 2020.
That, work on the design of the market was delayed and was expected to commence on July 1, 2020.
That, it was to toke approximately one month.
That, the allocation of stalls would be completed within four months of the construction being finished.
That in August 2021, Emonyo Yefwe International and the Dinah business community Petitioned The
Governor Bungoma county on the supposed roadside facility as being needed now more than ever as
one of the measures in response to controlling the corona virus pandemic.
That upto date, there has never been a response from the governor.
That Police hove denied us the right to demonstrate by refusing to give a permit.
That, these failures constituted human rights violations and further undermines, the Project's objective to
increase efficiency of rood transport along the Northern Corridor.

That, the delay to construct the market goes against the spirit of the pledge to 'leave no one behind",
relates closely to three important dimensions of the 2030 Agenda: poverty, inclusiveness and inequality.

That, the facility was to build the resilience of the poor and vulnerable; access to employment; and
expanding infrastructure with a focus on affordable and equitable access for all.

Therefore, as mobile traders ;-
We demand for the market construction to begin immediately.
We demand that KeNHA stops threatening traders with eviction until the market construction is completed
and traders relocated.
We demand the World Bank to convene a meeting between mobile traders and the Governor Bungoma
county.

 REF: RELEST FOR PERMIT TO HOLD PEACEFUL DEMOSTRATHON.
Dear sir,

The business community at Dinah intends to hold a peaceful demonstration as regards, delayed market
construction for mobile traders at Dinah Interchange, after completion of the Webuye Kitale road .

The decision to demonstrate comes after spirited efforts to engage the concerned authorities failed to bore
any fruits.

Emonyo fefwe international and the Dinah business community is of the opinion that the supposed
roadside facility is needed now more than ever as one of the measures in response to controlling the
corona virus pandemic.

Therefore, we ore appealing for your office to give us a permit as well as provide us with adequate
security on the material day.

The details of the concerns and efforts taken in view of addressing the issues peacefully are hereby
attached.

We intend to hold the demonstration on 23/11/2021 1

 REF: REQUEST FOR PERMIT TO HOLD PEACEFUL DEMONSTRATION

 Reference is made to your letter dated 22/11/2021 on the above subject matter.
 After perusal of the letter and wide consultation for the purpose of conducting of holding
 peaceful demonstration, I object your request based on the following points:-
 1.) Covid-19 pandemic is still enforced and people should discouraged on any public
 gathering.
 2.) Security threat against terrorism whereby they kill people en-mass and may take
 advantage of such gathering.
 3.) Traffic flow Dina is situated in a very busy Webuye - Malaba road and if allowed it
 will cause a major traffic obstruction.
 4.) If permit granted the peaceful demonstration may turned violent and cause of destruction
 of properties and loss of life.
 Therefore, I advise that you channel your grievances to the appropriate offices. e.g County
 Government and your local leaders within your areas. Demonstration is not a solution.
